l01.summary: Sehested refers to his letter to the king; Auersperg, at first surprised that no one came with full powers, took the matter up seriously on 14/24 Jan after conferring with La Fuente and gave the enclosed answer; Sehested asks the chancellor for the promised papers. P.S.: a breach between the Emperor and France is expected; forced levies; the French army put at 50,000; Rákóczi already in Poland, for himself rather than for Sweden; rumour of a Saxon marriage for the young king; Auersperg flatters Sehested and has attached Windischgrätz to him to sound him out.

l02.summary: To the king: Sehested greeted Auersperg on the alliance and the 'secret'; Auersperg took it ad referendum, then reported that the Emperor is not averse to the defensive alliance proposed by the king but expects the draft and conditions from Denmark; the 'secret' once mentioned to Castel Rodrigo no longer matters. On 14/24 Jan Auersperg asked for haste and for the inclusion of the States General.

l03.summary: To the king: nothing new; spirits in Vienna raised by Rebolledo's favourable report on Danish armaments, passed to the Emperor by La Fuente on 2/12 Feb; passage through Friuli refused to the Turk; the Swiss rejected France's threefold proposal (Alsace); birth of an archduke on 1/11 Feb; Rákóczi advancing in Poland, Danzig seeking neutrality.
l03.en:
Full translation (made at integration, 12 Nov 2026; square brackets mark symbol values that rest on the sense):

Since I have already several times given Your Royal Majesty a full and [most humble] report of my business here, I now rightly refrain from troubling Your Royal Majesty with repeating it once more, the more so as nothing particular has happened in it since and His Imperial Majesty only awaits your resolution with the greatest longing. Otherwise I find spirits here not a little raised, because by the last [post] [Rebolledo] sent [La Fuente] a wholly favourable report of Your Royal Majesty's armament and great preparations, and the said [La Fuente] at once laid it before His Imperial Majesty on the 2/12 of this month, whereby my news, which I had shortly before given to Auersperg, was in good part confirmed.

l04.summary: To the chancellor: the ministers await the resolution and full powers; ciphering has worn out his eyes, so no duplicates; news as in the letter to the king; his reports to Auersperg confirmed by Rebolledo. P.S.: talks in Paris with the cardinal; a Franco-Swedish offensive and defensive alliance is believed concluded.

l05.summary: To the king: the Emperor has consented orally to the cession of Bremen; should Sehested press for a written promise, and claim Bremen as a see or as a secularised duchy (better: hereditary)? The Turkish danger is played up; new patents for 7,000 men; an envoy is sent to [H].

l06.summary: To the chancellor: Auersperg would discuss Bremen only after the alliance; Sehested argues that Danish preparations are ready and that general peace is impossible while Sweden holds Pomerania, Mecklenburg and Bremen. On 11/21 Feb the Emperor, Auersperg and La Fuente conferred: the king will be satisfied; the Danish minister at The Hague should block ratification of the Swedish-Dutch treaty and bring the States General into the alliance. Auersperg then announced the Emperor's consent to the transfer of Bremen. P.S. at nine o'clock: the Emperor resolves on an offensive alliance and awaits the full powers urgently.

l07.summary: Proposition to Emperor Ferdinand III (audience of 18/28 Feb): Swedish possession of the duchies of Pomerania and Bremen endangers the Empire and Denmark and threatens the peace of Westphalia; if the king must carry his arms against Bremen, he hopes the Emperor will not oppose it and will support it with a diversion in Pomerania; he will wait for the Emperor's resolution and asks his advice and how far he may count on his help.

l08.summary: To the chancellor: on 18/28 Feb he presented to the Emperor the points of his new instruction (copy enclosed); the cession of Bremen was already granted; an answer on the diversion and effective cooperation is promised; the proposition goes to the privy council. P.S.: inclusion of the States General pressed; La Fuente wavers.

l10.summary: To the chancellor: the Emperor has resolved to conclude the offensive and defensive alliance quickly; Bremen better in Danish hands; send the full powers at once. Colonel Garnier secretly seeks help for Poland against Rákóczi; a secret imperial envoy urges Rákóczi to withdraw; the Emperor will act this summer, where is not yet known.

l11.summary: To the chancellor: Auersperg says the Emperor now wants a general offensive and defensive alliance binding both sides; Sehested took it ad referendum. The States General should come later as an accessory. Questions: should Denmark insist on 'Königliche Majestät' instead of 'Königliche Würden', on a recredential, and on a written promise for Bremen?

l12.summary: To the king: the Emperor stands by his first answer: nothing further before the king sends absolute full powers and an instruction for an offensive and defensive alliance; Bremen preferred in the king's hands; renewed advice on the States General, Poland, Danzig and other princes.

l13.summary: Memorial handed to Auersperg (?/9 March): Denmark can hold the Baltic and act on land; the Emperor is asked to declare himself on general peace while Sweden holds Pomerania and Bremen, on transferring Bremen to the king after its occupation, and on effective cooperation. If Sweden made peace in Poland it would recoup itself from Pomerania and Bremen 'mit den spoliis des armen Teutschlandes'. Sweden's attack on the city of Bremen against the imperial avocatoria has nearly forfeited the fief.

l18.summary: To the chancellor (cipher copy and clear of the time in the volume): Auersperg explains that the Emperor renewed the family pacts with Poland and promised troops, solely to second Denmark against Sweden, and calls this a sufficient diversion; on Bremen he advises the king to attack Sweden itself first so that Sweden opens hostilities from Bremen; Sehested answers 'praeuenire melius als das praeueniri'; Auersperg: 'multa fiunt et cogitantur quae non dicuntur'. The Emperor is gravely ill; the privy council asked to see Sehested's full powers.

l22.summary: To the chancellor: Hatzfeldt ordered into Poland with 12,000 men; his negotiation, which presupposed the late Emperor, is suspended; the news of 17/27 March was only meant to feed Denmark with light hopes, everything having long been concerted with Poland; an imperial councillor (Cridel or Lützow) may be sent secretly to Denmark to inspect the troops; 18,000 men decided for Poland. P.S. on the Swedish resident's insinuations.

l27.summary: French letter, Prague 3/13 Oct 1657, same cipher: the court will resolve either on full cooperation or on a strong diversion in Pomerania by the Poles, who will be given German troops after these are disbanded.
l27.en:
Full translation (made at integration, 12 Nov 2026; square brackets mark symbol values that rest on the sense):

... this court will resolve in the end either on a full cooperation or else on a powerful [diversion] in Pomerania by the Poles, to whom for this purpose a quantity of German troops will be given, after these have first been disbanded ... put in another memorial ...
